title: Zscaler's public AI Guard integration examples (zguard-ai-integrations): what the legacy reference recorded, pending a registered source

prose.text: Zscaler publishes example integrations that call AI Guard's DAS API from developer tools, gateways, cloud agent frameworks and CI pipelines. The repository is vendored here but not yet a registered source, so everything the legacy reference said about it is held as open statements to verify.

prose.label: Failure posture.
prose.text: Whether an integration fails open or closed depends on the host {{gap:fail-posture}}.

prose.label: SDK version.
prose.text: The repository's minimum Python SDK version is open {{gap:sdk-minimum}}; the SDK fix it points at is [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api:sdk-bearer]].

prose.label: The API they call.
prose.text: The DAS endpoints, host and direction values are in [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api]].

checks.do: Read the specific integration's own fail-open or fail-closed handling and its interception point before relying on it; the legacy notes differ by host.
That an explicit policy ID in an integration's configuration is numeric; malformed values may silently fall back to policy resolution.

catalog.title: What the zguard-ai-integrations repository covers
catalog.detail: Unverified legacy statement: zscaler/zguard-ai-integrations provides DAS examples for developer tools and IDE hooks (Claude Code, Windsurf, Cline), CI/CD (GitHub Actions), gateways, orchestration (n8n) and AI guardrail libraries, describing DAS as application-by-application wiring without proxy infrastructure; the September 1, 2026 head (release 0.2.0) added AWS Bedrock AgentCore, a boto3 hook, a Lambda decorator and Strands, OpenAI Codex CLI hooks, and Google Apigee X and Cloud Run. vendor/zguard-ai-integrations is vendored but is not a registered source in references/_meta/sources.json, so none of this can be cited; registering it and quoting at its pin would resolve or correct each point.

fail-posture.title: Which integrations fail closed, and their exceptions
fail-posture.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the root README presents a fail-closed default (ALLOW permits, DETECT is monitor-only, BLOCK blocks; missing keys, API errors, HTTP 401/403, HTTP 200 without an action, and unknown verdicts block), but the same README records exceptions: Windsurf and Cline post-hooks and the Codex Stop hook are audit-only, and unclassifiable gateway traffic passes unless failClosedOnUnknown is enabled. Codex Stop runs after the response has streamed, blocks on a BLOCK verdict, fails open on scan errors and skips short content. Windsurf pre-hooks allow traffic when AIGUARD_API_KEY is missing but fail closed on API errors. n8n documents fail-closed behavior only for its Continue On Fail path. The 0.2.0 changelog says the Claude Code hooks' fail-open paths (missing key, API error, exception, verdict-less response) were fixed, making older Claude Code file-read fail-open prose stale. vendor/zguard-ai-integrations is vendored but is not a registered source in references/_meta/sources.json, so none of this can be cited; registering it and quoting at its pin would resolve or correct each point.

host-timing.title: Where each integration intercepts and when enforcement happens
host-timing.detail: Unverified legacy statements: AWS Bedrock AgentCore scans prompt, response, tool input (before the tool runs) and tool output (before it re-enters the model) as tool events, awaiting async tools and draining generators first, with streamed-response granularity left to the caller. The Bedrock boto3 hook intercepts client calls before and after the operation and skips streaming responses at after_call. The Lambda decorator sees only one prompt and one response at the handler boundary; HTTP proxy events get 403 on a block, while direct and asynchronous invocations raise AIGuardBlocked to keep retry and dead-letter behavior. Strands hooks cover prompt, response, tool input and tool output: a blocked response can only request a retry and finally raises, tool input is cancelled before execution, tool output can be replaced only after the tool has run, streams may emit before the verdict, and Agent.structured_output() is outside the hooks. Codex hooks cover user prompts, Bash and MCP pre-tool input, Bash and MCP post-tool output, and Stop; apply_patch, other tools and stream interception are not covered, and post-tool hooks run after side effects. The Apigee inline proxy is synchronous and Gemini-only and blocks with HTTP 403; the SharedFlow covers Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, MCP and SSE and returns caller-shaped HTTP 200 refusals. Cloud Run pipelines deploy either pattern, the flow pipeline answering with HTTP 200 refusals and the proxy pipeline with JSON 403. vendor/zguard-ai-integrations is vendored but is not a registered source in references/_meta/sources.json, so none of this can be cited; registering it and quoting at its pin would resolve or correct each point.

static-defects.title: Defects and contradictions in the integration examples
static-defects.detail: Unverified legacy statements: the Strands README's constructor example has two bare policy_id= assignments and is invalid Python; the agentic integration guide labels Agent-to-LLM prompts OUT, scans llm_prompt with direction OUT and returns the generated response without a final scan, contradicting the architecture direction table and the AgentCore mapping (prompt IN, response OUT); the Bedrock response helpers discard the opaque-content flag and apply on_unscannable only when no text is extracted, so a mixed text-plus-image, document or unknown response may be scanned on its text alone; the Apigee SharedFlow MCP extractor copies only result.content[*].text, omitting non-text results; the Cloud Run README says the pipelines configure an existing Apigee organization, while the separate provision_org.py helper creates the organization, runtime, environment, group and attachments. vendor/zguard-ai-integrations is vendored but is not a registered source in references/_meta/sources.json, so none of this can be cited; registering it and quoting at its pin would resolve or correct each point.

policy-id-parsing.title: Malformed explicit policy IDs in the integrations
policy-id-parsing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the AgentCore, Bedrock boto3, Lambda and Strands helpers and the Codex utility strip quotes, attempt int() and return None for a malformed or non-numeric AIGUARD_POLICY_ID, so an invalid configured ID is treated as unset and auto-resolution runs, inconsistent with the root README's warning that a stale explicit ID can return HTTP 200 with no action and fail closed. vendor/zguard-ai-integrations is vendored but is not a registered source in references/_meta/sources.json, so none of this can be cited; registering it and quoting at its pin would resolve or correct each point.
